provenance.method: lesson notes written from the NERDC 2025 scheme of work outline; every week keeps its scheme topic and bullets as the teaching spine

topics.title: Nigerian folk songs
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to sing Yoruba folk songs.
The pupils should be able to sing Hausa folk songs.
The pupils should be able to sing Igbo folk songs.

Introduction:
Today we learn songs from our different tribes.
We have sung English songs before.

Content:
Folk songs are old songs from our people.
Yoruba folk songs have nice words like 'Àkàndé'.
Hausa folk songs sound like 'Mai shi k'aka'.
Igbo folk songs have words like 'Ọdịmma'.
We will sing in groups.

Class activity:
Group singing game.
Each group sings one tribal song.
Others clap to the beat.

Evaluation questions:
Name one Yoruba folk song.
Name one Hausa folk song.
Name one Igbo folk song.
Which group sang best?

Summary:
We learned many Nigerian folk songs today.

topics.title: Story songs
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to sing a story song.
The pupils should be able to act out a story song.
The pupils should be able to identify characters in a song.

Introduction:
We love stories in class.
Today we will sing stories.

Content:
Story songs tell a story with words.
Characters are the people in the story.
Chorus is the part we all sing together.
For example 'Tortoise and the birds' song.
We sing the story and move like the characters.

Class activity:
Story song drama.
Teacher sings the story.
Pupils act as characters.
Everyone joins in the chorus.

Evaluation questions:
What is a character?
What is a chorus?
Which story did we sing?
How did tortoise move?

Summary:
We sang and acted out a story song.

topics.title: Season songs
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to sing a rainy season song.
The pupils should be able to sing a dry season song.
The pupils should be able to identify rainy and dry seasons.

Introduction:
We know about rainy and dry seasons.
Today we sing about them.

Content:
Rainy season has many rains.
We sing 'Rain rain go away' song.
Dry season has hot sun.
We sing 'Dry season sun' song.
Rainy season brings fresh yams.
Dry season brings harmattan wind.

Class activity:
Season movement game.
When we sing rainy song we dance like rain.
When we sing dry season song we fan ourselves.

Evaluation questions:
What happens in rainy season?
What happens in dry season?
How does the rain song go?
How does the dry song go?

Summary:
We learned songs for both seasons.

topics.title: Tables chant
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to recite two times tables.
The pupils should be able to clap to the rhythm.
The pupils should be able to say tables in order.

Introduction:
We count numbers every day.
Today we count with a beat.

Content:
Two times tables are 2 4 6 8 10 and so on.
We say them with a strong rhythm.
Clap your hands for each number.
Two times one is two.
Two times two is four.
Two times three is six.

Class activity:
Tables march.
Pupils march around the class.
Clap and say tables together.

Evaluation questions:
What is two times three?
What is two times five?
How many claps for each number?
What comes after two times four?

Summary:
We learned two times tables with rhythm.

topics.title: Days and months songs
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to list the seven days.
The pupils should be able to list the twelve months.
The pupils should be able to sing days and months songs.

Introduction:
We come to school every day.
We have months in the year.

Content:
There are seven days in a week.
Sunday Monday Tuesday Wednesday Thursday Friday Saturday.
There are twelve months in a year.
January February March April May June July August September October November December.
We sing songs to remember them.

Class activity:
Calendar circle game.
Pupils stand in a circle.
Each pupil says one day or month.
We all clap after each one.

Evaluation questions:
How many days in a week?
How many months in a year?
What day comes after Sunday?
What month comes after July?

Summary:
We learned days and months with songs.

topics.title: Patriotic songs
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to sing 'Arise O compatriots'.
The pupils should be able to sing with pride.
The pupils should be able to identify Nigeria's national symbols.

Introduction:
Nigeria is our country.
We sing songs to show love.

Content:
'Arise O compatriots' is our national anthem.
We stand straight when we sing it.
We sing with strong voices.
The flag is green white green.
We love our country Nigeria.

Class activity:
Flag parade.
Pupils hold small flags.
March and sing the national anthem.

Evaluation questions:
What is our national anthem?
What colors are in our flag?
How should we stand when singing?
Why do we sing with pride?

Summary:
We sang Nigeria's national anthem.

topics.title: Call and response 2
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to do longer echo rhymes.
The pupils should be able to be a solo caller.
The pupils should be able to respond to calls.

Introduction:
We played echo games before.
Today we do longer ones.

Content:
Call and response is when one person calls and others respond.
Solo caller is the one who starts the song.
Echo means we repeat the words.
Longer echo rhymes have more words.
For example 'Hello class' 'Hello teacher'.

Class activity:
Group echo game.
One pupil is the solo caller.
The rest echo in response.
We make the rhymes longer each time.

Evaluation questions:
What is a solo caller?
What does echo mean?
Who will be the caller today?
How do we make longer rhymes?

Summary:
We did longer echo rhymes.

topics.title: Movement medley
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to sing while moving.
The pupils should be able to move through stations.
The pupils should be able to do freeze dance.

Introduction:
We love to move and sing.
Today we do both together.

Content:
Movement medley is many songs with movements.
Stations are different places in the class.
Freeze dance means stop moving when music stops.
We sing different songs at each station.
For example jump song at station one.

Class activity:
Station singing game.
Set up four stations with different movements.
Pupils move through stations singing.
Teacher plays music for freeze dance.

Evaluation questions:
What is a movement medley?
What happens in freeze dance?
How many stations are there?
Which movement did you like most?

Summary:
We sang and moved through stations.

topics.title: Class composed song
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to write a class song.
The pupils should be able to perform the class song.
The pupils should be able to add actions to the song.

Introduction:
We have sung many songs.
Today we make our own.

Content:
To compose means to make something new.
Our class song will be about our school.
We think of words together.
We add a nice tune.
We can add actions too.

Class activity:
Song making workshop.
Class suggests words about school.
Teacher helps make sentences.
Everyone practices the song with actions.

Evaluation questions:
What does compose mean?
What is our class song about?
Who suggested the first word?
What actions did we add?

Summary:
We made and performed our own song.

topics.title: Music festival
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to perform all year's songs.
The pupils should be able to sing in graduation.
The pupils should be able to remember song words.

Introduction:
We learned many songs this term.
Today we show what we know.

Content:
Music festival is when we perform all our songs.
We sing our Nigerian folk songs.
We sing our story songs.
We sing our patriotic songs.
We sing our class composed song.
We sing with big voices and smiles.

Class activity:
Graduation rehearsal.
Pupils stand in rows.
Each group performs their best song.
We practice walking on stage.

Evaluation questions:
What songs will we perform?
How should we stand on stage?
Which song is your favorite?
Why do we practice before?

Summary:
We practiced for our music festival.
